name: Street Perception of Residents and Tourists in Xi'an
description:
Method replication: same task, dimensions, scale and viewing rule as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (74 Baidu street views re-fetched inside the city walls of Xi'an, Mingcheng District, each stitched from four directions). Participants first say whether they are a resident or a recent tourist, then rate 50 random street views on five dimensions with 0–100 sliders (safety, comfort, convenience, pleasure, sociability, with the paper's definitions); each picture must stay on screen for at least 10 s before the ratings can be sent.

Original study: Kuang, Yang, Zhu & Chang (2026), PLOS ONE 21(3), e0345073. 15 residents of Mingcheng District and 15 tourists who had visited in the past 12 months rated stitched 3600×600 Baidu SVIs online, 50 images each, on the five dimensions (0–100, at least 10 s per image); random forest and SHAP models compared what drives residents' and tourists' perceptions across 5,309 images.

Differences from the original study: (1) images are newly fetched Baidu views, not the paper's images; (2) images are drawn at random rather than by the paper's stratified assignment that gave each image raters from both groups; (3) no researcher-led calibration with sample images, only written definitions; (4) a "neither" option and two background questions were added.
author: Kuang, Yang, Zhu & Chang
